rationale: The configured generic extcon framework must not reuse a connector ID until device_unregister has removed its device name. The release callback in pinned LTS is empty and object storage has separate ownership, so moving ida_free afterward does not dereference freed extcon storage. This prevents registration collisions without changing LTS lifetime rules.

The SDK uses ext4 and enables Unicode/casefold support. Pinned LTS still invalidates a casefolded dentry while holding a journal handle; eviction of child dentries can wait on that transaction, causing a deadlock. Stop the transaction before d_invalidate and guard invalidation on successful removal. The cherry-pick preserves all other newer LTS namei fixes and closes an availability failure.

F2FS remains enabled for Android configuration compatibility. Pinned LTS has the inline-directory conversion bounds check but lacks this lookup check. Reject an on-disk name length above F2FS_NAME_LEN or extending past the available filename slots before comparing it. This prevents out-of-bounds reads from malformed directory entries; existing LTS error cleanup and inode validation are unchanged.

The configured block scheduler permits concurrent sysfs scheduler changes. Pinned LTS retains the two-stage elevator_change/elevator_change_done sequence and a shared read lock, which permits concurrent kobject cleanup and memory corruption. Use the writer trylock for the whole switch, retaining the LTS trylock/EBUSY behavior that avoids the kernfs disk-deletion lock cycle.

Retain the generic and x86 POLYVAL/HCTR2 series as one coherent subsystem. Android configuration enables HCTR2. The new generic fallback avoids the old non-constant-time table implementation, and the x86 path preserves PCLMUL/AVX acceleration with an irq_fpu_usable fallback. ARM64-specific additions are excluded. Native LTS crypto fixes outside the selected series remain. Associated KUnit sources are retained but were not executed or enabled by the SDK build; no runtime claim is made. SECURITY.md records the known SDK AES-CTS storage policy and unresolved alternative HCTR2 use.

This intermediate rename allowed the old crypto_shash implementation to coexist with the new library during migration. The selected final series removes that old implementation entirely; the rename has no independent residual code or runtime requirement.

F2FS is enabled for Android filesystem compatibility. Propagate sync/checkpoint failures through directory-synchronous operations and a read-only remount instead of reporting success. Keep the native LTS unlink error label and earlier corruption cleanup; do not import the unrelated device-alias path from the ACK conflict side. In remount, clear SBI_IS_CLOSE before testing the sync error, preserving native LTS cleanup on failure before restore_gc. This avoids concealing durability failures without retaining an erroneous close-state flag.

In ra_data_block and move_data_block, LTS already acquires i_sem and igrab of the atomic inode before using its mapping, then iputs on success/error. Eviction uses the matching write lock before clearing the COW link. The port retains this protection together with its vendor bypass hooks.

LTS is_meta_ino already gates the synthetic compressed-cache inode on CONFIG_F2FS_FS_COMPRESSION and the COMPRESS_CACHE mount option. The port retains that check and the later rejection of inaccessible cached meta inodes.
LTS f2fs_move_file_range already stores the destination size as loff_t, checks LLONG_MAX overflow and calls inode_newsize_ok before extension. The port retains these checks with native LTS locking.

LTS already has do_zero_post_eof_page and the strict-mode writeback/error-return paths before size extension. Preserve its zeroing and writeback ordering to avoid stale post-EOF data after recovery; the ACK locking-context refactor is not required for this fix.

LTS __write_node_folio already passes folio->index to f2fs_sanity_check_node_footer, rather than comparing the node ID to itself. The port retains native LTS critical-error handling and this independent footer validation.

The pinned LTS already provides the transaction-lock snapshot and temporary target-thread reference in binder_free_transaction. Source comparison found that the initial port duplicated the acquisition; a658d19bb7fa removes that integration error. The final function equals native LTS plus the existing Android free-oem-structure hook, with one reference acquisition and one release. This preserves the UAF protection and avoids the leaked reference/racing second snapshot. C Binder remains a supported Android IPC implementation. See SECURITY.md: Binder lifetime reconciliation.

The pinned LTS already removes the incorrect direct unevictable-list transition in sort_folio and lets generic shrink/putback initialize mlock state. The port retains that flow and the later LTS dirty/writeback reactivation routine, with Android eviction hooks around it. This avoids stale poisoned mlock_count and LRU isolation races; no older ACK reclaim implementation replaces the LTS fix.

Retain page_ext_get/page_ext_put lifetime protection in the optional Android page-pinner implementation, including early-return releases, as part of the final ACK source integration. Native LTS page_ext lifetime API is used. Optional page-pinner necessity remains unresolved; it is retained for Android configuration/source compatibility, not asserted required by a found consumer. The old unprotected lookup must not be reintroduced. Runtime tracking behavior has not been tested.

The retained Android proxy scheduler must decrement nr_iowait on the source runqueue before proxy_set_task_cpu changes the task CPU. The final port does so and also retains later LTS task-on-CPU and blocked-owner validation before adjustment, preserving race protection. This avoids imbalanced I/O wait accounting across migrations; no runtime scheduler validation is claimed.

Retain Rust Binder reference cleanup outside the node_refs spinlock: declare cleanup owners before the lock guard, remove rbtree nodes with remove_node, and preserve death/freeze cleanup until after unlocking. This maintains Android Binder behavior while avoiding destruction of Node/NodeDeath references under the spinlock. Inspection of update_ref confirms the final ownership/drop order; native LTS shrinker-lock changes remain intact.

Retain the Rust Binder freeze-listener allocation retry: drop node_refs_guard before GFP_KERNEL vector allocation, reacquire and revalidate handle/cookie before modifying state, and defer the empty vector returned by remove_freeze_listener until outside the lock. The final node.rs/freeze.rs code includes this effect alongside later validation/logging changes. This prevents sleeping allocation/free under the node_refs spinlock and retains freeze notification semantics.

The memory-safety effect is already in LTS 81ea8e822185: retrieve bounded device pointers into a fixed local array and evict every device key before freeing it, without a failing allocation during key removal. The port retains native LTS get_devices signatures and F2FS device-count cap. Omit the ACK get_devices_new alias, obsolete callback slot and ANDROID_KABI_USE layout preservation, which exist solely for historical binary ABI.

LTS already keys its append-only mk_mode_keys list by HKDF context, cipher mode, data-unit size and encryption implementation. The port retains RCU publication, setup mutex, active-reference removal and later kzalloc_obj allocation. This prevents sharing a prepared key across incompatible data-unit sizes. Android wrapped-key flag compatibility is a separate retained change and does not replace the native LTS fix.

The SDK enables BLK_INLINE_ENCRYPTION_FALLBACK and DM_DEFAULT_KEY; native LTS __submit_bio invokes crypto preparation while current->bio_list is active, so recursive encrypted submissions can hold the resources an allocation awaits. Adapt the ACK rescue-list/workqueue fix to native per-page LTS allocation: nonblocking bio/page allocation in recursive submission, enqueue remaining source with its updated DUN, and retry outside recursion. When a partially filled bounce bio exhausts pages, submit it with an extra source completion reference before continuing; only an empty worker bio may block. This avoids both recursive-submit deadlock and waiting on pages held by the current partial bio without importing the bulk-mempool refactor. Preserve early LTS alignment validation, on-stack requests, native completion/error behavior and dm-default-key skip-bit propagation. Availability/security rationale and compile-only verification limits are in SECURITY.md.

Retain the ACK separation of pre-metadata resize failure from post-update failure. Local free_segment_range restores in-memory range counters before returning; failure before update_sb_metadata has not committed the resize. Restore user_block_count and clear SBI_IS_RESIZEFS without falsely setting NEED_FSCK. Errors after superblock/checkpoint modification still set NEED_FSCK, and LTS corruption checks and lock/freeze cleanup remain. This intentionally narrows the LTS repair flag to the error paths that can need repair, improving availability without suppressing detected corruption. F2FS is enabled for Android configuration compatibility.

The configured F2FS shrinker now checks freed < nr before reclaiming read-extent entries, just as it already does before NAT and free-NID reclamation. Preserve ACK runtime memory-pressure behavior and avoid unnecessary cache eviction; native LTS umount mutex/list synchronization is unchanged. No memory-safety improvement or measured performance gain is claimed.

F2FS compression and filesystem encryption are enabled. In the compressed-write error unwind, skip fscrypt bounce-page finalization if fio.encrypted is false; retain normal context/page cleanup. This avoids relying on internal fscrypt no-op checks for unencrypted pages. The old fscrypt helper already checks page mapping, so no existing exploitable defect is claimed.

Correct the F2FS inconsistent-segment diagnostic to identify the first printed type as SIT and the second as SSA, matching the actual arguments. Retain this small diagnostic companion to the GC review so corruption reports are interpreted correctly. No control flow, validation, storage behavior or security boundary changes.

Native LTS free_segment_range iterates every NR_CURSEG_TYPE, including in-memory current segments, before evacuating the range. The port retains this bound and native LTS resize cleanup with the separately documented transient-failure correction. This preserves the fix preventing active current segments from being left in a removed range.

Native LTS f2fs_gc_range accepts the lock argument, takes/releases gc_lock per section when requested, releases it on error/skip paths, and preserves early termination. The pinning caller requests this locking while already-locked resize callers do not. Keep the later LTS reset of pinned sections after collection. ACK lock-tracing wrappers are a separate unresolved feature review, not required to obtain this locking fix.

Native LTS pinning allocation propagates GC errors, syncs the filesystem to reclaim the space, and retries only after successful sync while clearing gc_required. The port retains this sequence together with per-section GC locking. No ACK replay is needed; this preserves availability and error propagation.

The pinned LTS routes node readahead through __get_node_folio with NODE_TYPE_NON_IXNODE, whose page-hit path calls f2fs_sanity_check_node_footer. The port retains this validation and newer footer checks/critical-error handling. A missing whole-patch textual match results from later LTS refactoring, not an omitted validation.

This ACK commit removes a duplicated packed-SSA initialization block introduced by an ACK merge. The pinned LTS and port init_sb_info each contain one sum_blocksize/sums_per_block/summary/journal initialization block, so the erroneous duplication is absent. Preserve native LTS initialization; no code application is necessary.

The entire patch adds android_kabi.h and ANDROID_KABI_DECLONLY(trace_eval_map) to stabilize symbol CRCs. The user explicitly excludes historical binary KMI. Native LTS types remain visible and Android network hooks are retained independently; no executable fix is omitted.

The entire patch adds android_kabi.h and ANDROID_KABI_DECLONLY(module) to preserve init_user_ns symbol CRCs. This is historical binary KMI bookkeeping excluded by the user. Keep native LTS declarations and the separate Android user hooks.

The final vendor_hooks.c keeps android_rvh_vmscan_kswapd_done before android_rvh_vmscan_kswapd_wake, as this ordering-only patch requests. Both export declarations remain. This is source organization, with no userspace/runtime or security behavior change.

Retain the set_user_nice_locked restricted vendor hook after acquiring the native LTS task runqueue lock and updating its clock. A registered trusted hook may modify nice or veto the update. The LTS CLASS(task_rq_lock) guard releases the lock even on the early veto return. This preserves Android source customization; hook implementations remain trusted kernel code, and no runtime hook consumer is asserted.

Native LTS converts PMSR freeing to wiphy_work, queues it on the wiphy and cancels it during wireless-device teardown before processing remaining aborts. The port keeps the updated callback signature, queue/cancel operations and init. This avoids the work/wiphy locking deadlock and preserves the later teardown cancellation fix.
